_comment: Authored grammar contrasts. Replaces the earlier auto-generated distractors, which were made by swapping two adjacent tokens and were frequently either still grammatical or obviously broken. Each pair targets a real error English speakers make, and carries the rule so the drill teaches rather than just tests. Vocabulary is drawn from seed_vocab.json where possible.

pairs.rule: Time expressions come before the verb, never after. English puts them at the end; Mandarin never does.
也 goes before the verb or adjective, not at the end.
很 precedes the adjective. Adjectives also don't need 是 — 我是累 is wrong too.
有 is negated with 没, never 不. This is the one irregular negation in Mandarin.
Negation goes immediately before the verb.
在 + place comes before the verb. English says 'work at home'; Mandarin says 'at home work'.
了 marking a completed action or change of state follows the verb.
Question words sit where the answer would sit. Mandarin doesn't front them the way English does.
的 attaches to the possessor: 我的宝宝, not 我宝宝的.
一起 is an adverb and precedes the verb.
Modal verbs (会, 能, 要, 想) come before the main verb.
Same time-before-verb rule, with a longer sentence to make it less obvious.
是 is a normal verb in second position, not a sentence-final copula.
For a past-tense 'didn't', use 没. 不工作了 means 'not working any more' — a change of state, not a past event.
想 as 'want to' precedes the verb it governs.
在 marking an action in progress goes before the verb.
太 precedes the adjective, and the pattern is 太 … 了 as a frame.
